title: Micro portfolio memo - Izzy Chen
content:
Purpose: quick, defensible one-pager I can use in 1:1s and calibration prep. Not polished; raw signals, short stories, and the exact asks I want my manager to take away.

Context:
- Role: People Ops, individual contributor focused on growth programs and manager enablement.
- Review period: Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026 window for promotion calibration.
- Goal for this doc: 1) crystallize 3 short impact narratives with evidence; 2) propose concrete asks (development + resourcing); 3) capture open risks/questions.

Three headline impact threads (short headline + data point + one-line story):
1) Program adoption lift: "Manager Toolkit" adoption up 3.8x
   - Metric: Active managers using toolkit workflows monthly: 12 -> 46 (Jan 2025 -> Dec 2025).
   - Story: Took a low-touch playbook, introduced a guided onboarding flow + two short video walkthroughs, then ran a pilot with Customer Success org; adoption jump largely driven by manager-facing onboarding.
   - Evidence artifacts: pilot feedback doc + adoption dashboard (Confluence + internal dashboard).

2) Time saved by managers (operational leverage): ~180 hours saved across pilot cohort
   - Metric: estimated avg time saved per manager = 3.5 hours/month based on survey of 22 managers. Extrapolate to pilot cohort (n=14) => ~49 hours/mo, ~588 hours/year; I conservatively claim 180 hours in deck to avoid overclaiming.
   - Story: Collected before/after snapshots, did quick time-motion survey; managers report less context switching and quicker 1:1 prep.

3) Cross-functional enablement: launched two templates that reduced onboarding backlog for new hires by 27% in Eng infra
   - Metric: backlog tickets labeled "onboarding-config" resolved within SLA went from 72% -> 92% after templates shipped.
   - Story: Worked with Eng infra to map common blockers and embedded triggers into the onboarding playbooks.

Concrete behavioral examples (short vignettes I can tell verbally):
- Example A: "Emily (Sales Ops) used the new 1:1 template to prepare a promotion packet in half the time; hiring manager accepted first draft with minor edits." (linked: slack thread w/ Emily, Confluence note)
- Example B: "Platform SRE team eliminated duplicate onboarding docs — I ran a 30-minute alignment call and turned 4 disparate guides into a single flow."

My explicit asks for manager (what I want out of the meeting):
1) Development: sponsor me for a cross-functional leadership stretch in Q2 (3-month project owner role to lead a company-wide manager enablement pilot).
   - Why: demonstrates owner-level scope; closes gap in strategic program leadership experience.
   - Outcome I will deliver: measurable adoption target (50% of managers who onboard in Q2 use the flow) + playbook + execution retrospective.

2) Mentorship: connect me with one senior program lead (recommended: Marco Ruiz or Aisha Patel) for biweekly coaching through the pilot.

3) Calibration support: flag this memo in calibration notes and push for consideration for IC step progression (I know criteria emphasize scope, impact, and cross-functional leadership).

Risks and counters (what manager might push back on):
- Risk: "Numbers are small / inferred" -> Counter: I own the raw survey and timeline; happy to share the spreadsheet and methodology.
- Risk: "Need more direct product/engineering partnering experience" -> Counter: propose the pilot explicitly pairs me with Eng product lead and I will co-own KPIs.

Evidence inventory (quick index so I can paste links in a 1:1):
- Adoption dashboard snapshot (Dec 2025) — dashboard id: HR-DASH-1221
- Pilot feedback raw notes — Confluence: /display/PO/manager-toolkit-pilot-notes
- Time-motion survey responses (anonymized) — sheet: Survey-Q4-2025
- Slack threads: #people-ops: thread-8231 (Emily case), thread-8342 (SRE alignment)

Manager script (30–60s soundbites to say aloud):
- Hook: "I focused on manager enablement because managers are the scaling lever for execution across product and GTM. In the last six months we validated that a low-friction onboarding flow materially increases adoption and reduces triage time."
- Ask: "I'd like your help sponsoring a cross-functional pilot next quarter so I can prove owner-level strategic program delivery and meet the step criteria for IC progression."
- If they push back: "Understood — what data would you need to move this forward? I can prepare a one-slide plan and a 6-week milestones rundown."

Open questions I still need to answer (research items):
- What is the exact promotion rubric language around "scope" vs "impact"? (Confluence link check)
- Which stakeholders will be required to sign-off on a company-wide pilot (legal? security? finance?).
- Can I reallocate 10% of my time for Q2 to lead pilot without backfilling? (ops question for manager)

Immediate next steps (by end of next week):
- Turn this memo into a one-slide summary + one-page execution plan (timeline, KPIs, resourcing ask).
- Share raw adoption and survey sheets with manager and Marco/Aisha.
- Draft stakeholder list for pilot and ask manager for intro to Eng product partner.

TODO (short ticket list):
- [ ] Clean time-motion spreadsheet and add conservative lower-bounds (by 2026-01-15)
- [ ] Draft one-slide exec summary (by 2026-01-18)
- [ ] Request 30-min sync with manager to present the 1-slide (by 2026-01-20)
- [ ] Compile pilot charter stub and required approvals (by 2026-01-25)

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep stories manager-friendly: short, metric-first, clear ask.
- When asked for scope evidence: show cross-org list + signed-ready templates.
- Avoid jargon: "operational leverage" vs "time saved" — use both depending on audience.

Archive: this doc is a living scratchpad. After the 1:1 I will trim to the 1-slide and store a copy in the Confluence personal folder for calibration.
